stories.headline: Goff Wins It Late for THE MACHINES
stories.dek: Settled in the fourth. THE MACHINES 106.08, Lil’ Chops 100.38.
paragraphs: They played a tight one. Tight is the word for it. Tight like a bad shoe. THE MACHINES 106.08, Lil’ Chops 100.38 — 5.7 points in it.
The one that did it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Jared Goff, an 8-yard touchdown pass, and that put THE MACHINES in front at 105.48–100.38. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Chris Rodriguez — a 25-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 8.5 to THE MACHINES.
THE MACHINES got there on Puka Nacua (18.7), Lamar Jackson (18.4), Jared Goff (14.2). Aaron Rodgers answered with 22.0 and it was not quite enough.
Somewhere a front office is staring at a bench score and hoping nobody noticed.

stories.headline: Master-Jeti Hold Off Killer Klowns
paragraphs: Not a classic. Not a disaster. One of the other ones. Master-Jeti 118.02, Killer Klowns 105.2, a 12.8-point margin.
The one that did it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Jake Bates, a 43-yard field goal, and that put Master-Jeti in front at 109.02–105.2. Nobody took it back.

The biggest single play of the week belonged to Treylon Burks — a 47-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 10.7 to Master-Jeti. That is the play people will remember, which is unfortunate for everyone else.
Master-Jeti got there on Kenneth Walker (29.9), Jake Bates (18.0), Seattle Seahawks (14.0). Kyren Williams answered with 26.7 and it was not quite enough.

Killer Klowns left Keon Coleman and his 17.6 on the bench and started Marcus Mariota, who returned 4.4. That is 13.2 points sitting in a chair. and yes, before you ask, that would have won them the football game. I would not bring it up at the next meeting.
Not pretty. They all count the same.

stories.headline: Beaver Eaters Hold Off BIG BLUE
paragraphs: Workmanlike. Businesslike. Several other kinds of like. Beaver Eaters 138.94, BIG BLUE 114.12, a 24.8-point margin.
The one that did it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Bryce Young, a 32-yard touchdown pass, and that put Beaver Eaters in front at 118.98–114.12. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Malik Nabers — a 25-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 8.5 to Beaver Eaters.
Beaver Eaters got there on Javonte Williams (26.3), Bryce Young (18.9), Malik Nabers (17.2). CeeDee Lamb answered with 24.3 and it was not quite enough.
BIG BLUE started Travis Kelce and got 1.5 points for the trouble. A lovely painting in a burning house.

Beaver Eaters left Drake Maye and his 26.8 on the bench and started Christian Watson, who returned 4.7. That is 22.1 points sitting in a chair. It would not have changed the result, which is the only consolation available.
My producer is telling me to move on, and for once he is right.

stories.headline: Pork Chop Express Leave No Doubt
stories.dek: Pork Chop Express 100.22, Wookie Leaks 58.62. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: This one was decided early and then kept going anyway, which is the worst kind. Pork Chop Express 100.22, Wookie Leaks 58.62, a 41.6-point margin.
Wookie Leaks had the lead early and then watched it leave. By the time it mattered there were 41.6 points in it, and the only question left was whether anybody was still watching.
The one that did it came in the third quarter, the Sunday late games: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, a 28-yard catch, and that put Pork Chop Express in front at 43.26–41.62. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Brock Bowers — a 20-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 8.0 to Pork Chop Express.

Pork Chop Express got there on Matt Gay (16.0), Brock Bowers (14.6), James Cook (14.3). Jacoby Brissett led Wookie Leaks with 11.1, which on an afternoon like this one is a lovely painting in a burning house.
Wookie Leaks started Rashee Rice and got 0.0 points for the trouble. The box score says he played. The box score has been wrong before, but not this time.

Pork Chop Express left Kyle Monangai and his 27.0 on the bench and started Jalen Nailor, who returned 0.0. That is 27.0 points sitting in a chair. It would not have changed the result, which is the only consolation available.
The good news is that it is over. That is the entire list of good news.

stories.headline: The Powers of Pain Handle Smoke Dragons
stories.dek: The Powers of Pain 135.8, Smoke Dragons 100.64.
paragraphs: Never close enough to be interesting, never far enough apart to turn off. The Powers of Pain 135.8, Smoke Dragons 100.64, a 35.2-point margin.
The one that did it came in the first quarter, the Sunday early games: Nico Collins, a 45-yard catch, and that put The Powers of Pain in front at 13.5–12.6. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Bijan Robinson — a 59-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter, Monday night, worth 11.9 to Smoke Dragons. Put that one on the tape and keep it.

The Powers of Pain got there on Nico Collins (23.8), C.J. Stroud (20.1), Brock Purdy (19.3). Bijan Robinson led Smoke Dragons with 26.7, which on an afternoon like this one is a lovely painting in a burning house.
Smoke Dragons started Cooper Kupp and got 1.3 points for the trouble. Somebody is going to have to answer for that at the next meeting.

Smoke Dragons left Brian Robinson and his 24.7 on the bench and started Cooper Kupp, who returned 1.3. That is 23.4 points sitting in a chair. It would not have changed the result, which is the only consolation available.
Somewhere a waiver claim from August is feeling pretty good about itself.

stories.headline: StillTheCream Survive the Back-and-Forth
stories.dek: 10 lead changes. StillTheCream had it last, 96.9–78.06.
paragraphs: Now this one I enjoyed, and I say that about almost nothing. StillTheCream 96.9, Guido Haters 78.06, an 18.8-point margin.

They traded it 10 times. Every time one of them looked like getting clear the other one answered. It took most of Sunday to shake out. There were 10 touchdowns between them, and none of them settled a thing until the last one did.
The one that did it came in the first quarter, the Sunday early games: Luther Burden, a 7-yard catch, and that put StillTheCream in front at 14.26–13.96. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Emanuel Wilson — a 23-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 8.3 to Guido Haters.
StillTheCream got there on Ka'imi Fairbairn (16.0), Rhamondre Stevenson (15.4), Jordan Love (13.1). Emanuel Wilson answered with 24.0 and it was not quite enough.

Guido Haters left Romeo Doubs and his 17.8 on the bench and started Kendre Miller, who returned -0.1. That is 17.9 points sitting in a chair. It would not have changed the result, which is the only consolation available.
I aged a year on that one and I was already old.

stories.headline: Kamara Wins It Late for n.W.o
stories.dek: 10 lead changes. n.W.o had it last, 85.26–76.34.
paragraphs: Back and forth all afternoon. My scorekeeper asked to be relieved. n.W.o 85.26, Phins Phag 76.34, an 8.9-point margin.

They traded it 10 times. Every time one of them looked like getting clear the other one answered. It ran right through to the night games. There were 9 touchdowns between them, and none of them settled a thing until the last one did.
The one that did it came in the fourth quarter, Monday night: Alvin Kamara, a 3-yard touchdown run, and that put n.W.o in front at 80.56–76.34. Nobody took it back.
The biggest single play of the week belonged to Chuba Hubbard — a 15-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter, Sunday night, worth 7.5 to Phins Phag.
n.W.o got there on Will Reichard (19.0), Alvin Kamara (17.8), Patrick Mahomes (16.5). Chuba Hubbard answered with 24.9 and it was not quite enough.
A game like that is why I switched to the second drink. I regret nothing.

stories.headline: Horsecollars Make It Hurt
stories.dek: Horsecollars 119.6, Gumbas 60.14. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: Some games are contests. This was a chore. Horsecollars 119.6, Gumbas 60.14, a 59.5-point margin.

Gumbas did not lead at any point in this football game. Not once. There is no sequence to describe because there was no sequence — Horsecollars scored first and then kept scoring, and the rest was arithmetic.

The biggest single play of the week belonged to George Kittle — a 56-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 11.6 to Gumbas. That, friends, is a career highlight. I would know — mine was a walk.

Horsecollars got there on Tetairoa McMillan (31.2), Jonathan Taylor (21.7), Zay Flowers (17.8). Tyquan Thornton led Gumbas with 23.1, which on an afternoon like this one is a lovely painting in a burning house.
Gumbas started Samaje Perine and got 0.7 points for the trouble. He was out there. I can confirm he was out there.

Horsecollars left Isaiah Williams and his 13.3 on the bench and started Kalif Raymond, who returned 0.6. That is 12.7 points sitting in a chair. It would not have changed the result, which is the only consolation available.
File it, forget it, and let us never speak of it again.
